Level 2 - Beginner 40 min AWS Networking

AWS Networking: VPC, CIDR, Subnets, Route Tables, IGW and NAT

Build your own private network inside AWS: pick an address plan that never collides, split it into public and private subnets in every Availability Zone, write the route tables, and follow one packet from the internet all the way to a private Kubernetes pod. If you have ever configured a router, this is home ground.

sections.title: The story: a gated apartment complex
What a VPC is: your own network inside a region
CIDR planning: pick address ranges that never collide
Public, private and isolated subnets, one of each per AZ
Route tables and the Internet Gateway
NAT gateway: outbound-only internet for private subnets
VPC endpoints: reach AWS services without the internet
Packet walk: from a phone on the internet to a private pod
Build it: the VPC as code
Production: many VPCs, flow logs and cost traps
